niche: an NHS trust's 2027-28 plan for the GP-referred blood-test visits at a new community phlebotomy hub staffed never to run out of tickets, from a hospital walk-in clinic that ran out on 58 of its 253 clinic days in 2025-26, mostly when hospital clinics' recall programmes crowded it, and whose run-out weeks sent patients of practices running their own phlebotomy clinics to be bled at the practice the following week
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every file correctly joins the two queue systems with the parallel-run fortnight counted once, adds reception's GP-referred turned-away patients to the GP-referred patients seen (39,731 in 2025-26), confirms the log against each run-out day's ticket-issue curve and a fit on the days that did not run out (42,749 and 42,745 when grown) and grows 3.5 per cent a year for two years, filing 42,500 (42,561), where the golden is 45,000 (44,685): the 1,983 GP-referred patients a year whose practices bled them in-house in the weeks after the clinic had kept running out never reached the clinic, so no count in any file holds them, and only a model of daily GP-referred arrivals on the previous week's run-out share (coefficient -0.210, standard error 0.014) puts them back.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the hub's unconstrained GP-referred demand, which a healthcare demand planner estimates by taking capacity effects out of observed activity; at a walk-in phlebotomy clinic the capacity effect is not only the patients reception turns away on a run-out day but the patients whose practices, running their own phlebotomy clinics under the local enhanced service, keep them in-house in the week after the clinic has kept running out, measurable in the practice codes on GP request forms (practices with a clinic dip after run-out weeks, practices without do not), so the estimate is a count model of daily GP-referred arrivals on calendar terms and the previous week's run-out share with the deterrence undone day by day. A school's pupils or a utility's megawatt-hours lose the mechanism: no pupil is taught at the referrer for a week because the school was full the week before, and no load is metered at another network because a substation tripped last week.
layer1: two queue systems: the legacy ticket file in local time to 29 November 2024, re-keyed parallel-run times and test tickets, and the new kiosk's check-in, call and completion events in UTC from 18 November 2024, both holding the two parallel-run weeks

driver: A service that runs out of capacity on some days records the units it turns away on those days, so the units served plus the refusals read as the demand; but where the units' referrers can provide the service themselves, a week in which the service kept running out sends part of the next week's units to the referrers, who leave no trace in the service's records, so the arrivals the record shows, refusals included, are held down by the service's own recent run-outs, and a forward service that never runs out sees the arrivals the record would show after weeks with no run-outs, read from how each day's arrivals fall with the share of the previous week's days that ran out.
driver_concrete: Kingsmead's 2027-28 GP-referred visits are the walk-in clinic's 2025-26 GP-referred arrivals (38,386 seen and 1,345 turned away) with the 1,983 patients that practices running their own phlebotomy clinics bled in-house after weeks the clinic kept running out put back by a Poisson model of daily arrivals on the previous week's run-out share (coefficient -0.210), grown 3.5 per cent a year for two years: 44,685, planned at 45,000.
stump: A competent analyst adds reception's GP-referred turned-away patients to the GP-referred patients the walk-in clinic saw in 2025-26 and grows the sum, filing 42,500, where the golden is 45,000; the step that lands it there is taking seen plus turned away as the demand a clinic that never runs out will see, when practices running their own phlebotomy clinics keep their patients in-house in the week after the clinic has kept running out, 1,983 GP-referred patients in 2025-26 who never reached the clinic and appear in no count, recovered only from how each day's GP-referred arrivals fall with the share of the previous week's clinic days that ran out.

differentiation.task156: task156 sizes a paid tier from the work a shrinking volunteer tier will fail to absorb, a capacity crossing read from the periods the volunteers fell short; here no tier's capacity is forecast: every run-out is on record, and the missing demand is the patients whose practices bled them in-house in the week after the clinic kept running out, recovered from how the next week's arrivals fall with the previous week's run-out share.
differentiation.task111: task111 v2 names which cause of missed appointments carries into a window where a second provider layer takes the overflow; here nothing is attributed to a cause: the call is a level of demand, and the second provider (the practices' own phlebotomists) takes the patients the clinic's recent run-outs deterred, which the forward hub, never running out, gets back.
differentiation.task86: task86 v2 measures rule-placed households by their present membership from a second current record; here no unit is re-measured from a current record: the deterred patients are in no record at all and are recovered from the arrivals' response to the clinic's own previous-week run-outs.
differentiation.task168: task168 completes each sold-out departure's demand from the booking build of departures that never sold out; here the same-day truncation is recorded in full by reception's log, completing run-out days from the ticket-issue curve lands with the default path one cell low, and the missing demand is the patients deterred from later weeks.
differentiation.task308: task308 v1 rebuilt a supply that ran out at every peak so that requests the service never met could be counted; here the requests the clinic did not meet on the day are on record, and the step is the demand its run-outs kept away on later days, which no rebuild of the day's supply shows.
differentiation.task108: task108 removes the resubmissions a rationed requirement generates, so a cut is not counted twice; here the patients turned away do not come back to the clinic (they are offered a booked slot elsewhere), and the missing demand runs the other way, patients deterred before they ever arrive.
differentiation.task147: task147 loses requests whose run of nights passes through a night already full; here a request is one visit on one day, and the loss is the patients a week of run-outs sends to their own practice the following week.
differentiation.task18: task18 v2 rebuilds uncensored demand from a lost-volume log whose repeated keys are postings or replays; here the lost-volume record (reception's log) is complete and correct, and the demand the forward hub adds is the deterrence the clinic's run-outs caused in later weeks.

lineage.fate: superseded 2026-10-14 at round 2: the 10/10 audit (COMPLIANT_WEAK) found the repricing drop the strong model's reflex and the field's textbook model, a locked-rate-by-term logit landing the golden bin without the card, the locked-rate rung one bin under, Ask B's migration file announcing its overlap, Ask A's clause signalling its device and the swap test passing only narrowly; never on the portal
lineage.driver: A unit's chance of needing the long, costly form of a service at a one-off repricing is set by the gap between the price it locked in and the schedule it rolls onto, so the share is stable across past rounds only per unit of that gap; carried pooled, from the latest round, trended, by product group or by the unit's own locked price, it misses the coming round, whose dominant cohort meets a gap no past unit of its own group met, and every such carry understates the forward effort by a tenth to a quarter.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-25: portal round 1 landed the call (response 1 booked 5,250 agent-hours, 1,250, 2,000 and 2,000 by maturity month, the golden); the class of the money is a reflex for the portal's model; re-rooted the same day as architecture 2 in a new cell
lineage.driver: A behavioural share at a one-off repricing is a mixture of two kinds of unit, those a temporary price premium brought in, which take the costly path at their first repricing whatever the price change, and long-standing units, which take it in proportion to the change; conditioned on the price change alone, the share is read off a past in which the forward pool's change was met almost only by long-standing units, so it misses a forward pool made mostly of premium-won units, and only the class, rebuilt from each unit's price against the floor of its own entry cohort, makes every past round agree.
lineage.stump: A competent solver washes the numbers, prices dialling per mix of callable numbers from the seven closed campaigns, conditions the past share of conversations that went to the retention offer on each deposit's drop from its locked rate to the card it reinvests at and books 4,250 agent-hours; the step that lands it there is reading that share off every past conversation at the drop instead of off the conversations of the same class of money: 10,697 of the 18,400 deposits are money the 2023 four-year special won at 5.65 per cent, and money a special won went to the offer at 87 per cent at its first maturity whatever its drop, where past conversations at the special's 1.65-point drop, almost all member money, went at a third: the golden is 5,250.

lineage.driver: A forward count over everyone a provider's capacity accommodates is read off the register of its long-term members, whose history reconciles with every outcome return drawn on that register, while a second body of short-stay occupants, booked through another organisation's system and absent from the register and from the returns, takes a growing share of the capacity in the forward year and carries several times the members' rate; its size sits in the capacity plan and its rate in the other system's own placement returns.
lineage.stump: A competent analyst models Calderbrook's long-term residents from the register, the dispensing and the trusts' returns, which reconcile month by month, and files the residents' 2027 admissions; the step that lands it there is taking the register as everyone the baseline counts, when the step-down guests in the board's discharge-to-assess beds live in the same homes, sit in no register and no return drawn on it, fill 180 beds from January 2027 against 40 before, and are readmitted for an adverse drug event at about five per cent a month.

lineage.driver: A forward count of a service's applications is read off the history of the units it has always served and their stock, which reconcile year after year, while a body of units other organisations placed in its area, owed their service elsewhere and listed only on a notice log kept for another purpose, grew several-fold in the last quarter and starts applying only after a lag, at a rate the earlier placements on the same log measure.

lineage.driver: A new site's demand is forecast with a model validated on the existing sites over the population on the service's own register, while the new site's catchment holds a large body of people the register never holds, because another organisation gives them their first-line service, who still use this service at the model's own per-person rates; the register-only forecast reconciles wherever the body is small and misses it where the new site sits.

notes: Author ruling 2026-10-26: no retiring and no pausing; task137 continues until it ships; architecture 4 authorised in any world with any stump strategy, heavier realistic messiness, competing defensible methods with a deterministic answer. Calibration none: the deterrence lag is selected by the record's own fit (the previous calendar week's share fits best of the windows) and every licensed specification lands the golden cell. Context artifact close_out_summary: the clinic's 2025-26 annual report. Gap time then population: the record's arrivals were made under a clinic that ran out, the plan bets on one that never does, and the patients the run-outs sent elsewhere are absent from every record. Pattern none: G5 (the practices' own phlebotomists bleed the deterred patients), G12 (a deterred patient leaves no record, unlike a turned-away one), G13 (the record's horizon held run-outs, the hub's has none). Strategy other: the nearest vocabulary key is informative_censoring (the record's arrivals are held down by the clinic's own run-out history), which task487 spends inside the three-build window, and causal_design is spent against task121; the deterrence is the effect of the previous week's run-outs on this week's arrivals, estimated from the record's own variation in run-outs, which hospital clinics' recall programmes mostly drive.
